source.title: Large Language Models Implicitly Learn to See and Hear Just By Reading

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extends scaling to image and audio classification using text-pretrained backbones and reports downstream accuracy across backbone sizes. It does not measure pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream accuracy results across multiple text-backbone sizes, which bear on V6. Its discussion of language-model scaling laws and its citation of Kaplan et al. are not results testing those laws. The frozen-versus-LoRA comparison is not extracted because it compares tuning setups rather than performance across scale.
record.test_reason: The study LoRA-tunes text-pretrained GPT-2 backbones of 2–3 sizes for image and audio classification and reports accuracy by backbone size. This is a new downstream setting bearing on V6's 'improves with scale' part. It fits no power law and does not relate results to pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that text-pretrained LLM weights, LoRA-tuned with small learned front ends, give competitive image and audio classification with few trainable parameters. They say scaling the text backbone boosts accuracy across modalities, 'consistent with' Kaplan scaling laws, though they fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: The study transfers text-pretrained GPT backbones to image and audio classification, using learned modality front ends and LoRA; it does not fit language-model pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy varies with backbone size across the evaluated datasets; no sensitivity to scaling-law fitting choices is tested.
record.problems: The scaling evidence is limited to a few backbone sizes per dataset and downstream accuracy metrics; no uncertainty estimates, power-law fits, or out-of-range predictions are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The scratch-trained, frozen-backbone, and ViT results in Tables 1–4 were not extracted because they are not additional text-backbone scaling points for V6.

untested.parts: Whether gains are predictable (no fit or extrapolation), and any relation to pretraining loss; only 2–3 sizes per task, no uncertainty.
All; no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form under transfer or fine-tuning; no loss fits, only accuracy at a few sizes.

missing.what: Larger text backbones are said to converge faster during fine-tuning on FSD-50K (training curves by size).

record.verdict_notes: Evidence for scale is thin: 2–3 sizes per task, no error bars, and trainable parameter counts grow with backbone size. The text overstates the FSD-50K gain (about 4% claimed vs 2.7 points in Table 4). The text also says sizes go 'to nearly one billion', while Table 4 lists 1.5B. Scratch, frozen and ViT rows were correctly left out as non-scaling comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss is measured against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run loss fit or prediction of larger-run loss is reported.
No fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is measured.
The paper does not compare architecture depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Image and audio tasks are included, but the paper does not test whether held-out loss follows the same power-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
The paper reports downstream accuracy by backbone size, but does not fit a predictive relation or compare downstream performance with pretraining loss.
No scaling-law fit choices, exponent sensitivity, compute-optimal split, or bending of fitted curves is studied.

relationships.condition: LoRA-tuned GPT-2 backbones (87M–1.5B) transferred to CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, GTZAN and FSD-50K classification
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises monotonically with backbone size in all four sweeps (+0.8 to +2.7 points; r2, r4, r6, r8, r9 vs r1, r3, r5, r7). Gains are small, single-run, and confounded by differing LoRA parameter counts.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased at every tested backbone size across all four sweeps by 0.8–2.7 points, with single-run comparisons confounded by differing LoRA parameter totals.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
